newsitem.title: CANADA: Gaz Metropolitain to build $230 million gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Gaz Metropolitain to build $230 million gas pipeline.

text.p: Gaz Metropolitain said Friday it plans to build a 136-mile (220-kilometre) natural gas pipeline between Lachenaie, Quebec, and the New Hampshire border at a cost of C$230 million ($170.3 million).

The project, to be conducted on behalf of TransQuebec & Maritimes Pipeline, a company in which Gaz Metropolitain and TransCanada PipeLines are equal partners, will supply the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System.
The pipeline will also bolster the natural gas distribution system in the Estrie region, in response to growing demand.

The Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, a project in which Gaz Metropolitain and TransCanada also have a stake, will carry Canadian natural gas to markets in New Hampshire, Maine and as far as Boston.
Construction is set to begin on Dec. 1, 1997, and the pipeline is scheduled to be in service on Nov. 1, 1998.
